headline: Simulators and physical priors constrain learned models of biological patterns
label: Simulation Constrained Biological Pattern Learning
summary: Learned models now embed simulation, symmetry, and view statistics as modeling constraints for shape and pattern generation.
synthesis: The common thread is an explicit physical, geometric, or environmental prior that constrains a learned model. DiffeoMorph learns SE(3)-equivariant graph neural network agent rules end-to-end through a differentiable agent-based simulator, scored by a 3D Zernike shape-matching loss for morphogenesis. The bacterial pattern study conditions a diffusion model on a coarse PDE model of P. aeruginosa colony growth, using it as a spatial prior to generate realistic synthetic patterns. The perception study is less directly simulation-based: transformers trained on embodied visual experience acquire shape perception, with view diversity identified as the driver and retina-like image transforms aiding learning. What is new is that simulation, symmetry, and view statistics serve as the modeling constraint itself.
